sources.entry: Databunker - Network-based, self-hosted, GDPR compliant, secure database for personal data or PII. (Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Databunker is a self-hosted, Go-based API service for tokenizing and storing personal data (PII/PHI/KYC) with encryption and GDPR-oriented features.
summary.what_it_does: Databunker stores personal records behind a REST API and returns UUID tokens that applications can use to reference them instead of keeping the data in the main database. The README says records are encrypted with AES-256 and that search uses hash-based indexing. It states it blocks SQL and GraphQL injection by design and keeps bulk retrieval disabled by default. It lists GDPR data-subject operations (right of access, restriction/consent withdrawal, erasure, rectification, portability) as built in, plus consent management and an audit trail. The README says it supports MySQL and PostgreSQL and includes an OpenAPI specification and a Docker image for running a demo. A Node.js SDK is shown in an example.
use_cases: Tokenize and store user PII outside the main application database
Back a KYC process for a crypto or financial startup
Handle GDPR data-subject requests such as access and erasure
Keep audit trails of customer profile changes
Replace a user table with an API-based record store
Store temporary identities for secure data exchange
how_to_run: curl -s -X POST -H "X-Bunker-Token: DEMO" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"first":"John","last":"Doe","login":"john","email":"user@gmail.com"}'  (create a user record against the demo instance)
notable: Tokenization: returns UUID tokens to reference personal records from application code
Hash-based indexing for searching encrypted records
Built-in GDPR request handling (access, erasure, rectification, portability, consent withdrawal)
Passport.js support is listed in the README
caveats: Credit-card tokenization and enterprise security features are described as part of a separate paid 'Databunker Pro' offering
The README's resource and demo links are empty in this text, so setup beyond the Docker demo is not fully documented here
Compliance claims (HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC2, ISO27001) are stated marketing-style and not independently verified in the README
keywords: alternative to hashicorp vault for pii
